target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum; docs/flora-annotation-playbook.md compound shapes): lanceolate (PATO_0001877) – linear (PATO_0001199)
reason: A run-together spelling of lanceolate-linear, a compound of two shape values. The playbook reads it as a continuum between the two.

Mucroniform means shaped like a mucro: the part itself is a short, abrupt, stiff point (a tubercle, a style base). That is not mucronate (FLOPO:0991054), which describes a part that ends in a mucro. Pointed is the nearest existing term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) + pink (PATO_0000954)
reason: This is the colour of a region of the part, not a quality of the whole part. Rose means pink, and it applies to the apex of the bract or petal.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md, two statements of one bearer: viscid (PATO_0001370) and pilose (FLOPO:0991048)
reason: It combines two existing values: pilose and sticky. Both hold of the same part, so they are two statements, not a continuum and not a new term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum): triangular (PATO_0001875, EXACT synonym deltoid) – subulate (PATO_0001954)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two shape values: a triangular base drawn out into an awl-like point. The compound-shape rule covers it.
These are two comparisons with another part, given as alternatives. Rows that do not name the second part ('scale: equaling or exceeding') stay unresolved, like 'shorter'.

PATO lists oval as a synonym of ovate, so the compound reduces to ovate. The botanical sense of oval as broadly elliptic would make this a continuum elliptic–ovate, but both readings fall within ovate outlines.
It states that the branch or axis bears spikelets. The words 'from the base' describe position and belong to the record, not the class.

target: docs/odp/15-absence-of-a-part.md (leaf PO_0025034 absent) with the qualifier of docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md
reason: This is leafless, which is the absence of a part, softened by 'almost'. The approximation stays in the RDF record. It must not become a firm absence axiom, so the record should go to review.
A comparison stated without its second term, like 'paler' and 'smaller' in the previous review.
Lepidote already maps to scaly (rule C235). 'Densely' is a degree, and 'pale' and 'appressed' are separate qualities of the scales. A full phrase does not justify a new term.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (towards the containing part, e.g. perigynium, oogonium)
reason: This is a relation between a part and the cavity that contains it, and it needs the second part. PATO has no relational 'filling' quality, so until one exists the record is RDF only.
A hyphenated compound of two existing margin values: serrate with deep, irregular, lacinia-like teeth.
It means having a distinct marginal band. The narrowness is a degree of the band. A separate statement could give it (margin of the part, decreased width), but it needs no new term.
The existing value closed with an approximation cue, the same as '±' and 'sub-'.
It means somewhat fleshy: a degree of fleshy, not a separate texture. Semi-woody got its own class because it means woody in some parts and herbaceous in others, which is not true here.
Unguiculate is already a synonym of clawed. 'Short' describes the length of the claw and can stay in the record.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum): square (PATO_0000413, approximate per docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md) – ovate (PATO_0001891)
reason: A compound of two shape values, the first with the 'sub-' approximation.
'Sub-' before an existing value is the approximation pattern.
In Bromeliaceae descriptions it means covered with minute scales that look finely tomentose. Lepidote maps to scaly (rule C235), and the tomentose look comes from the scales, not from hairs.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md, two statements of one bearer: transparent (PATO_0000964, synonym hyaline) and yellow (PATO_0000324, approximate per docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md)
reason: It means translucent with a yellowish tinge: two existing values, transparency and colour, held by the same part.

Bicolour leaves have two surfaces of different colour, and bicolour scales have a centre and margin of different colour. Both fit discolorous, whose definition covers compared surfaces or parts. Multi-colored (PATO_0001533) is variegated patchwork, which is a different thing.
The definition of repand already says shallow, irregular, rounded sinuses, so 'irregularly' adds nothing.
Gland-dotted has glandular-punctate as a synonym, and this is the same words in the other order.

target: primary root (PO_0020127, synonym tap root) present
reason: An axonomorphous root system is a taproot system, dominated by a persistent primary root, and PO lists tap root under primary root. Presence of a primary root is weaker than persistent dominance, hence medium confidence.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): trichome (PO_0000282) + brown (PATO_0000952)
reason: A phrase, not a word: the trichomes on the part are brown. As in the previous review's ruling on 'covered', the covering carries the quality.
It means reticulate with very small lumina, used of pollen exine. The fine size is a degree within reticulate, so a rule is better than a palynology-specific term.
Flimsy corm tunics, scales and peduncles are thin, weak and easily broken or torn. Fragile is the nearest disposition; the word is loose, hence medium confidence.
A negation of amplexicaul, which is PATO clasping (FLOPO:0991066 was replaced by it).

Three-sided stems and fruits are triangular in cross-section; trigonous has three-angled and triquetrous as related synonyms. For flat calyx teeth, triangular (PATO_0001875) may be the intended sense.
